In cause list, it appears that designation i.e. SC-I is missing along with the name of Sri xxxx, learned counsel for the respondent No.xx.
Office is directed to publish the designation also along with the name of Sri xxxx, learned counsel for the respondent in the cause list.
Let this matter be listed on xxxx.
(Arun Kumar Rai, J.) Pramanik/ Bail

The instant revision application is directed against the order dated 15.01.2022, passed by learned Sessions Judge, Seraikella, whereby the Cr. (Bail) Appeal No.
29 of 2021 preferred by the juvenile petitioner for bail against the judgment dated 02.12.2021 in Rajnagar P.S. Case No. 62 of 2018, corresponding to G.R. No. 813 of 2018 (S), passed by the learned Principal Magistrate, Juvenile Justice Board, Seraikella, which has been rejected.
3. Precise submission has been made on behalf of the revisionist that he is facing enquiry before Juvenile Justice Board, Seraikella and he is in custody since 28.08.2018.
He has further submitted that maximum punishment under Juvenile Justice Act is prescribed three years and he is languishing in custody since 2018.
On the aforesaid premise, he prays for bail.
4. Mr. Shiv Shankar Kumar, learned APP on behalf of the State conceded to the fact that petitioner is in remand home since 28.08.2018.

5. Without going into merits of the case, considering the judicial detention of juvenile, the petitioner is directed to be enlarged on bail, on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Ten thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Principal Magistrate, Juvenile Justice Board, Seraikella in Rajnagar P.S. Case No. 62 of 2018, corresponding to G.R. No. 813 of 2018 (S), on the condition that one of the bailers must be father of the petitioner.

2. Petitioners have been made accused in connection with Deoghar (Cyber) P.S. Case No. 85 of 2023 for the offences registered under sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code and sections 66(B), 66(C), 66(D) and 84 (C) of Information and Technology Act,

Deoghar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. On 17.12.2023 Cyber Police, Deoghar on the basis of confidential information, raided the hut of Nakul Ray.
It was alleged that he was a cybercriminal.
When they reached near the hut of Nakul Ray, on seeing them, three persons started fleeing away.
They were caught and they spelt out their names as Nakul Ray, Umesh Ray and Karu Marik.
Subsequently, on search, mobile phones and e- gadgets were recovered from their possession.
Later on, house of the petitioner Pankaj Das and other petitioners were raided.
They were apprehended and from their possession also, mobile phones and e- gadgets were recovered.

4. Mr. Shailesh Kumar Sinha, learned A.P.P appearing in one of the cases, after going through the case diary, submits that as far as the petitioners Pankaj Das, Raj Kishor Das and Umesh Ray are concerned, statement of three victims were recorded in which they have stated that they were cheated by the holders of the mobile phones which were recovered from the possession of Pankaj Das, Raj Kishor Das and Umesh Ray.

5. Mr. Sudhansu Kumar Deo, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner Umesh Ray submits that the only allegation against him is that he had chat with one Rahul Kumar on WhatsApp and it does not appear from the WhatsApp chat that he was trying to cheat these persons.

6. Mr. Lalit Yadav, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner Pankaj Das, submitted that his complicity has also come in the WhatsApp chat with the victim which suggest that he had not cheated anybody.

7. Mr. Shailendra Kumar Tiwari, learned Special P.P. submitted that mobile phone which was used by the petitioner Umesh Ray was used in cheating the victim of Rs. 4,000/-.
8.
At this stage, Mr. Shiv Shankar Kumar, learned A.P.P has pointed out that the petitioner Pankaj Das has cheated one victim of Rs. 4,000/- 3.
9 Considering the aforesaid facts, I am not inclined to enlarge the petitioners Pankaj Das, Raj Kishor Das and Umesh Ray on bail.
Accordingly, their prayer for bail stands rejected.

10. However, considering the aforesaid facts, I am inclined to release the petitioners Vikas Kumar Das, Nakul Ray, Aslam Ansari, Raju Kumar Das and Karu Marik on bail on Sukhu Oraon vs The State Of Jharkhand .....
